subject: Data Engineering
title: Data Quality Dimensions
description: A micro-lesson that makes Data Quality Dimensions usable.

hook.text: Saying 'the data is bad' isn't specific enough. Bad how? Data quality has six measurable dimensions.

buildup.text: Accuracy: is it correct? Completeness: are values missing? Timeliness: is it up to date?

discovery.text: Consistency: do sources agree? Uniqueness: are there duplicates? Validity: does it follow the rules?

twist.text: Data can be accurate but stale, complete but inconsistent. Each dimension fails independently.

climax.text: Naming the dimension lets you measure, track, and fix the specific problem instead of guessing.

punchline.text: You can't fix 'bad.' You can fix 'stale' or 'incomplete.'

quiz.question: Which is NOT one of the six data quality dimensions?
